title: Kenyan Plain Coconut Rice
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN039 is a quicker, plainer version of the full Wali wa Nazi (KEN021). Where KEN021 uses cardamom, cinnamon, and a more complex ratio, this version is the everyday quick coconut rice — just coconut milk, water, salt, and rice. Perfect as a simple weeknight side.

desc: Plain Kenyan Coconut Rice — basmati rice cooked in a simple blend of coconut milk and water until each grain is perfectly fluffy and subtly fragrant. The everyday weeknight version of the classic coastal Wali wa Nazi.
longDesc: Not every meal needs the full ceremony of spiced Wali wa Nazi. Sometimes you want that gentle coconut fragrance in under 30 minutes — a simple, clean rice that pairs with anything from grilled fish to coconut chicken curry to a simple bean stew. This is that rice. Pure, fragrant, fluffy, and effortless.
steps: Rinse the rice until water runs clear. Drain well.
Combine coconut milk, water, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add the rice and stir once.
Reduce heat to lowest setting. Cover tightly.
Remove from heat. Rest covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve.
chefTips: Rinse the rice thoroughly — removes excess starch for fluffier grains.
The 10-minute rest is essential — do not skip it.
commonMistakes: Too much liquid — makes the rice mushy.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Freeze for up to 1 month.
reheating: Sprinkle with a little water and reheat gently or microwave covered.
healthBenefits: Provides sustained energy from complex carbohydrates.
Coconut milk adds healthy medium-chain fats.
culturalNote: Plain coconut rice is the everyday workhorse of Swahili coastal cooking — always present alongside grilled fish, curries, and bean stews. It is one of the first dishes Kenyan coastal children learn to make.
cookingScience: The ratio of coconut milk to water (roughly 1:1) provides just enough fat to coat the rice grains and prevent clumping, while the water provides the steam needed for gentle gelatinisation of the starch.
sustainabilityTips: Use leftover coconut rice in rice salads or fried rice the next day.
